description: Local threat-signature database for sentinel-scan. 'hashes' are exact file-content matches (SHA-256/MD5). 'patterns' are regex content signatures for common malicious indicators found inside scripts/text/binaries. Extend this file (or point --db at your own) to add coverage; 'sentinel-scan update-db <file>' merges a new feed in.

hashes.name: EICAR-Test-File
hashes.description: Industry-standard EICAR antivirus test file. Not real malware; used to verify scanners detect and respond correctly.

patterns.name: EICAR-Test-String-Embedded
patterns.description: EICAR test string found inside file content (file may be larger than the canonical 68-byte test file).

patterns.name: PowerShell-EncodedCommand
patterns.description: PowerShell invoked with a long base64-encoded command, a common obfuscation/delivery technique.

patterns.name: PowerShell-Download-Cradle
patterns.description: PowerShell download-and-execute cradle, frequently used by droppers/loaders.

patterns.name: PHP-Obfuscated-Eval-Webshell
patterns.description: Obfuscated eval() commonly used by PHP webshells to hide payloads.

patterns.name: JS-Obfuscated-Eval
patterns.description: Obfuscated JavaScript eval() often used to hide malicious script payloads.

patterns.name: LOLBin-Certutil-Download
patterns.description: certutil abused as a living-off-the-land downloader.

patterns.name: LOLBin-Mshta-Remote
patterns.description: mshta.exe fetching and executing a remote HTA payload.

patterns.name: Embedded-Base64-PE-Header
patterns.description: Base64-encoded Windows PE ('MZ') header embedded in a script or text file — indicates a smuggled executable payload.

patterns.name: Ransom-Note-Language
patterns.regex: your (personal )?files (have been|are) encrypted|to (decrypt|recover) your files|pay(ment)? in bitcoin
patterns.description: Language typical of ransomware ransom notes.
